7.11.1.1 Investigator Symptom Score TheFor subjects treated at the hospital/study center, the investigator will use a symptom score to assess the severities of symptoms of acute cutaneous, abdominal, and laryngeal attacks of HAE using the following 5-point scale. Symptom scores will be recorded on Day 1 at pretreatment and at predetermined time points after treatment. Results will be recorded in the CRF. Investigator-rated Symptom Score 0 = none; absence of symptoms 1 = mild (no to mild interference with daily activities) 2 = moderate (moderate interference with daily activities) 3 = severe (severe interference with daily activities) 4 = very severe (very severe interference with daily activities) For attacks classified as cutaneous and/or abdominal, investigator-rated symptom scores will be collected for 8 symptoms: abdominal tenderness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, skin pain, erythema, skin irritation, and skin swelling. For attacks classified as laryngeal, investigator-assessed symptom scores will be collected for 13 symptoms: abdominal tenderness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, skin pain, erythema, skin irritation, skin swelling, dysphagia, voice change, breathing difficulties, stridor, and asphyxia.

7.11.1.2 Home Healthcare Provider or Parent/Legal Guardian/Caregiver Symptom Score The home healthcare provider or parent/legal guardian/caregiver, after having received appropriate training, will assess the severities of symptoms of acute cutaneous, abdominal, and laryngeal attacks of HAE using the 5-point scale provided in Section 7 11 1 1 Symptom scores will be recorded on Day 1 at pretreatment and at predetermined time points after treatment. Results will be recorded in the CRF. For attacks classified as cutaneous and/or abdominal the home healthcare provider or parent/legal guardian/caregiver-rated symptom scores will be collected for 8 symptoms: abdominal tenderness, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, skin pain, erythema, skin irritation, and skin swelling. For attacks classified as laryngeal, the home healthcare provider or parent/legal guardian/caregiver-assessed symptom scores will be collected for 13 symptoms: abdominal tenderness nausea vomiting diarrhea skin pain, erythema, skin irritation, skin swelling, dysphagia, voice change, breathing difficulties, stridor, and asphyxia Section impacted by change: Section 7.11.2 Subject Self-assessment of Pain Revised Text: FPS-R self-assessment data will be recorded in an e a diary. Subjects will record self-assessments on Day 1 at pretreatment and at predetermined time points after treatment while at the hospital/study center, and after their discharge to home. . Subjects will return the e diary to the hospital/study center at the scheduled visit on Day 8. 8.2.1 Pretreatment (Baseline) Assessments (Day 1, No Attack) The following assessments will be performed for subjects who will be treated with icatibant in the absence of a current HAE attack. 8.3 Pretreatment (Baseline) Assessments (Day 1, Initial and Subsequent Attacks) The following assessments will be performed at both initial and subsequent icatibant treated attacks unless otherwise indicated. All evaluations and sample collections must be performed prior to treatment. • Medical history (at initial attack only) • Confirm inclusion/exclusion criteria • Pubertal status determination (only if the subject was classified as prepubertal at the time of the screening visit) • Menstrual cycle history (in pubertal/postpubertal females only) • Physical examination • Vital signs • ECG (at subsequent attacks only) • Height and weight • Subject self assessment of HAE related pain (in subjects 4 years of age and older) using e diary FPS R • Investigator assessment of HAE symptoms • Investigator assessment of HAE related pain (in subjects younger than 4 years of age only) using FLACC • Clinical laboratory tests (serum chemistry, hematology and urinalysis) Icatibant (FIRAZYR) Clinical Trial Protocol Amendment: HGT-FIR-086 18 March 2016 Shire Confidential 100 • Urine pregnancy test (in females of childbearing potential) • Reproductive hormone assessments • Pharmacokinetic sampling (at pretreatment for initial attack only) • Immunogenicity evaluation • Recording of concomitant medications • Assessment of adverse events (at pretreatment for subsequent attacks only)

8.6 8.4 Subsequent Icatibant-treated Attacks (Pubertal/Postpubertal Subjects Only) Pubertal/postpubertal subjects may receive treatment for up to 2 subsequent HAE attacks, contingent upon having been treated forreceived an initial attackicatibant treatment and presenting with a subsequent acute attack of at least 73 days after prior treatment (see Section 4.1.3). Each treatment for a subsequent attack will require a Day 90 follow up visit. If a subsequent attack occurs within 7 days of the Day 90 follow up visit for the previous attack, the assessments on Day 8 and Day 90 will be combined.

3.1 Study Overview Modified the dosing in the Fludarabine, Cyclophosphamide, and ALLO-647 arm to be FCA-90 (ALLO-647 90 mg total dose; 30 mg/day x 3 days), and deleted the FCA-60 dose and ALC-based dosing requirements. Sponsor has determined the FCA-90 regimen to be optimal based on clinical response rates and safety tables, supported by the PK/PD data.

Synopsis; 3.1 Study Overview; 5.1 Allocation to Treatment; 9.3.5 Randomization; Changed the randomization stratification factor to be based on the risk factors LDH and tumor lesion size: Stratum 1: ULN < LDH ≤ 2 x ULN and presence of lesion ≥5 cm Stratum 2: LDH ≤ ULN or all lesions <5 cm The stratification factor is intended to balance randomized subjects across the 2 arms with less favorable disease characteristics of higher baseline LDH and bulky tumors.

Synopsis; 2.2 Objectives and Endpoints Modified Secondary Objectives and Endpoints by moving ALLO-647 PK/PD and host T cells, and ALLO-501A cellular kinetics, and immunogenicity of ALLO-647 and ALLO-501A from Exploratory to Secondary. To reflect the additional components of investigating ALLO-647’s role in enhancing effectiveness of CAR T therapy.

Synopsis; 8.5 Data Safety Monitoring Board; 9.2 Sample Size Determination Added the DSMB’s review of SAEs for enrollment pausing criteria will occur after have been randomized and had the opportunity to be followed after the first dose of lymphodepletion. Providing additional information regarding the DSMBs activities in monitoring safety in an ongoing manner throughout the study, including the potential to pause enrollment. 4.2 Exclusion Criteria The following Exclusion Criteria were modified or added: • Clarified that untreated latent tuberculosis is ineligible. • Unstable arrhythmia. • History of solid organ transplant (corneal transplant permitted). • History of hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH). • History of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). • Clinically significant liver disease, including viral or other hepatitis or cirrhosis. Clinically significant pulmonary disease, such as severe COPD; bronchospasm requiring intubation; interstitial lung disease, or pneumonitis (drug-related or autoimmune). These additional exclusion criteria provide further clarification that subjects with unstable or medically severe conditions, or a history of adverse reactions, may be unsuitable for CAR T therapy and are excluded.

5.12.3 Anti-Infective Prophylaxis CMV-seropositive subjects on the FC arm may receive letermovir at the investigator’s discretion. Although CMV-seropositive subjects receiving the anti-CD52 antibody ALLO-647 are at the greater risk of CMV reactivation and should receive prophylaxis with letermovir, subjects receiving FC-alone may also be at risk, and may receive letermovir at the investigator’s discretion.
